title.narrative: Guinea-Bissau: Solar Energy Scale-up and Access Project

description.narrative:
The electricity access rate in Guinea-Bissau, currently at 33 percent, remains low compared to neighboring countries such as Senegal, The Gambia, or Guinea. This requires government or public-sector intervention as a development priority to ensure both increased access and improved energy delivery across the country. Electrification projects, despite their significant development benefit, are often not commercially viable. This is because the initial consumption of those newly connected tends to be low, especially in more remote areas with lower population density. As a result, there are usually insufficient income streams to cover capital or operational costs for this kind of medium- to large-size infrastructure project. While consumption of those newly connected will likely increase over time, with increased ability to pay, such a business model is generally not attractive for the private sector.
The underlying conditions and sector fundamentals for private-sector participation are currently lacking in Guinea-Bissau. There is a need to increase private-sector participation in the development and operation of generation projects also in view of the weak financial standing of the national utility and limited fiscal space in the country. Therefore, public sector financing is needed to set up the conditions for a gradual increase in the participation of the private sector in generation projects, mitigating the high risk currently perceived by potential IPPs. To decrease such risk and ensure that the private sector financing is mobilized in a cost-effective manner, the project will support the preparation of feasibility studies, environmental and social safeguard studies, site permitting and preparation, investment in grid reinforcement to integrate variable renewable energy, including in battery energy storage systems, transaction advisory to support structuring and tendering bankable solar projects, and provide guarantee support from the Green Climate Fund (GCF).
One of the key objectives of the Solar Energy Scale-up and Access Project (SESAP) is to enable solar power generation in Guinea-Bissau by facilitating private sector participation and federating support from other development partners.
The project will support Guinea-Bissau's key energy policy objectives to increase electricity access and improve electricity supply. The SESAP project aims to support improving the reliability and affordability of power supply in Guinea-Bissau and maximize the number of households provided with electricity services while fostering local economic industrial development as well as attracting private investment. Improved access to electricity will also act as a facilitator for the delivery of public services and industrial development beyond the city capital of Bissau. Through this project, competitively procured solar power will be harnessed to deliver energy services and simultaneously diversify the energy mix in a country dominated by HFO and diesel-based power generation. The project will therefore strengthen energy security and contribute to decreasing CO2 emissions, as well as increase electricity access through investments in the T&D infrastructure. The project is in line with the least cost development plan and will complement regional energy projects under implementation.
The project will include grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) and the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and will have three main components including a Contingency Emergency Response Component (CERC): (i) Development of solar energy generation and network enhancement, including site preparation for utility-scale solar parks in Bissau, and Bafata, reinforcement and extension of the distribution infrastructure to integrate additional solar energy, and supporting and increasing solar-based energy access, including developing of mini grids in the Bijagos islands, solar PV solutions for health facilities and productive uses, and reinforcement of the distribution infrastructure to connect new households; (ii) capacity building, technical assistance, and project implementation support; and (iii) a CERC to provide the needed space for quick responses to natural disasters or health crisis.
The project development objective is to enable solar power generation and increase access to electricity in Guinea Bissau.
